John Wilder Tukey ( / ˈ t uː k i / ; [ 3 ] June 16, 1915 – July 26, 2000) was an American mathematician and statistician , best known for the development of the fast Fourier Transform (FFT) algorithm , the box plot and for laying the foundations of the field of exploratory data analysis . [ 4 ] The Tukey range test , the Tukey lambda distribution , the Tukey test of additivity , and the Teichmüller–Tukey lemma all bear his name. He is also credited with coining the term bit and the first published use of the word software .
